title: Regulated rail fares freeze (England), 2026
registry_rule: The reform specification for the 2026 regulated rail fares freeze. This file stages NO value claims: the DfT saving figures in circulation are DfT's, and the #86/#91 re-publication rule applies — a re-published figure belongs to its originator, and is harvested in its own lane from primary documents, never copied from reporting into a spec.

engine_pin.pin_rule: Read from importlib.metadata at write time, never typed as a literal. v1 of this spec hardcoded 2.89.2 — copied from a sibling spec — while the readings actually came from the installed engine. A typed pin is not provenance; --resolve refuses a mismatch.
engine_pin.pin_meaning: The engine this registry's readings were VERIFIED against. It is not the compute version — the certified bundle pins ==2.89.2 (see compute_engine_constraint).

direction_note: The freeze is ALREADY IN the certified baseline — gov.dft.rail.fare_index carries it. So the scored object is the COUNTERFACTUAL: what fares would have done under prior law. The engine ships that leg too, as gov.dft.rail.prior_law_fare_index. This is the indexed-baseline problem #13 and #67 keep meeting, except here we do not have to construct the counterfactual — the engine already carries both legs, and the comparison is baseline vs counterfactual rather than baseline vs reform.
mechanism_note: rail_usage x fare_index -> rail_subsidy_spending -> dft_subsidy_spending. The factorisation is deliberate and documented in the engine: rail_subsidy_spending's docstring states it exists 'allowing reforms to modify fare prices independently of usage quantity'. So a fare-price change is expressible without touching the usage quantity.

scope_conditions.regulated_share_note: Regulated fares are a MINORITY of tickets sold in England. A DfT passenger-level saving and a PE household-level subsidy aggregate therefore measure different populations. This is recorded here as a named divergence axis (#59) BEFORE any comparison runs, so a gap is attributed to scope rather than to the engine.
scope_conditions.entity_mismatch: DfT reports savings per passenger; the engine's quantities are per household. The two are not the same denominator and a counterpart must state which it publishes.

not_yet_run: This PR specifies and resolves the reform; it computes no counterpart. UK counterpart compute runs through #51, which is not merged. Publishing a number before that lands would bypass the compute contract.

compute_engine_constraint.note: The certified bundle DECLARES its own engine compatibility: policyengine-uk ==2.89.2. So a compute of this lane runs at 2.89.2 regardless of what is installed for verification, and re-computing at a newer engine needs a NEW certified bundle, not a pin edit. engine_pin is what the paths were re-read against; this is what the run must use. They differ, and the registry says so rather than implying the newer engine is usable end to end.
compute_engine_constraint.readings_hold_on_both_engines: Verified across BOTH engines, not assumed: the readings first committed on 2026-08-27 under 2.89.2 (fare_index 1.217/1.268/1.318, prior_law 1.288/1.342/1.394) are byte-identical to the 2.92.0 re-resolve. So 2.92.0-verified readings are safe for a 2.89.2 compute.
